plan.english: The great hero harnessed the swift horses, and they went to the dragon's field. There he cried out, "Serpent, come forth! My spear is thirsty." Then the dragon saw him and was afraid. His spear pierced the dragon, and it died. So he won imperishable fame.

Two brothers harnessed the swift horses. This one drove the chariot, and that one grasped the spear. The earth trembled under the wheels. An enemy stood and said, "Where are you going?" "We are seeking fame." Then that one killed him.

The king gave the hero a gift. "I will bring you the head of the wolf." Then he went out into the night. The wolf heard him and ran against him. But he seized the wolf and split its head. He carried the head to the king. He said, "Your name is famous."

Many came to the settlement at night. This one broke the door, and that one put fire into it. It burned. The king stood in the door and said, "I am not afraid of fire, and I will not flee from them." Then he killed the first of them, and the others fled.
Dawn became bright, and the wheel of the sun rose over the earth. The hero rose and yoked the horses to the yoke, and he said, "Swift horses, carry me!" The horses heard him and ran forward.

A man stole the shepherd's cattle. The shepherd told the hero, "They are gone." "I will find them." He yoked his horses and followed the man's path. At dawn he saw him and the cattle. He hurled his spear, and the man fell. Then he led them home.

The wounded hero lay on the earth. His brother came and sat beside him. The hero said, "Brother, I shall die, but my fame will live. Take my spear and do not cry out." Then sleep took him, and he became famous.

title: The hero calls on the gods

plan.english: The hero stood on the field and spoke to the gods. "Father Sky, hear me! Give me good fame and swift horses. Perkʷunos, you who hurled the spear at the serpent, be friendly to me." Then the gods heard him, and he went forth and was not afraid.

A wild horse was standing. No one had come near it. A hero came, looked at the horse, and said, "I shall yoke you. You will carry me, and I will give you water." The horse stood up and the hero led it away. Then they went forth, and the horse became famous.

Someone came to the smith. He said, "Make me a spear." The smith worked. He heated the spear and struck it. It was adorned and strong. "Take it. Do not give me a gift. Your fame will be my reward." He took the spear and went away.

Three men came to the sea. It was broad, and it was getting dark. Then the first said, "Dear ones, do not tremble. We shall go over the sea and seek fame." They went away. It swallowed them, but their fame is imperishable.
The man came at dawn. His wife saw him and said, "Husband, you have come! Where were you?" "I bring you gifts and fame. Sit down, wife, and eat." Then she became glad, and they sat down.

title: The man who broke his oath

plan.english: Two made an oath by the sky. This one kept the oath, but that one lied and took his cattle. Then the first said to him, "You who broke the oath, you shall not live. My spear will find you." He hurled the spear, and that one died.
A son was born to the hero. He took him in his arms and said, "I shall give you a name." "May your name be great, and may your fame be imperishable. Gods, protect him." Then the gods heard him.

Two men stood opposite each other on the road. This one said, "Who are you, and where are you going?" That one answered, "I am strong, and I am famous. Go away from my path!" "I shall not leave. The path is broad. If you seek my death, stand up and take your spear." They hurled their spears, and that one sank down.

They stood by the horses. This one said to that one, "Hear me! My horses are swift, and my wheels are strong. Let us drive to the sea. Whoever arrives at the sea will take the prize." "Your words are many, but I drive. Yoke your horses!" They went, and the earth trembled under the wheels. That one reached the sea and took the prize.

Many men stood on the field. This one stepped out in front and cried, "Who will come against me? My spear killed men. I fear no one." "Your words are many, but my spear will drink." That one came against him, and this one fell.

A hero stood and cried out to the dragon, "Serpent, hear my words! My spear is strong, and my heart is strong. You devour cattle and sheep, and you are the enemy. Come forth, or I shall come to you!" The dragon came out and said, "Many fell by my fang. You will die." He hurled his spear, and the dragon's head was split. So he won good fame.

The king spoke to the hero, "Give me your horses and cattle, or I shall take them and burn your settlement." He heard and answered, "I will not give you my horses, and my cattle will not go to you. If you come against me, you will see my spear." The king came, but he saw the spear and fled.

Two brothers were sitting and drinking. This one said, "I am the first and I am strong. I shall take the spear." "You are the first, but I killed the wolf. Stand, and take your spear." The mother came and said, "Do not strike your brother! Is the field not broad?" They heard her and put down the spears.

The enemy fled, and that one cried after him, "Where are you going? Yesterday your words were great. Now your heart trembles. Stand and take your spear!" This one answered, "I shall not stand, for I shall live." "Go, then. Whoever flees, his name is not famous."

Two stood there. This one said to that one, "You stole my cattle." "I did not steal." "Then swear the oath by Sky." That one swore the oath and said, "If I lie, may Sky kill me." But he was lying. Sky heard, and he died.

A wolf came to the sheep in the night. The dog heard him, stood up, and said, "I guard the shepherd's sheep. Go away, or you will see my fangs." "You are the shepherd's dog, but I am free. You work for the shepherd, and I work for no one." The dog said, "The shepherd feeds me, but you tremble." That one went away into the night.

Two sat down before the king. This one said, "I killed seven wolves in the night." "I split the head of a serpent. It devoured sheep and billy goats." The king heard them and said, "You are both great. To this one I give a spear, to that one I give a horse."

This one said to his enemy, "At dawn I shall stand on the field. Come with your spear." "I shall come. May the sun see us." Dawn became bright, and they stood on the field. They hurled their spears, and that one sank down.

Two came. "Who are you? I do not know you." That one answered, "Your father was a guest in my father's home." This one said, "Then you are my guest, and I will not kill you. Put down your spear, and let us give gifts. Take my horses, and I shall take your spear." So they gave gifts, and they became famous.

A strong hero stood at the door of the settlement. He cried out, "Whoever comes to this door will see my spear." Then the hero of good fame came. He said, "Stand aside from the door, or I shall break it." The strong one did not move. He hurled his spear, and the strong one fell. Then he broke it and went into the settlement.

title: The hero takes leave of his wife

plan.english: The hero stood by his chariot and said to his wife, "Wife, I am going out from our home, and I shall seek fame. Sit, and guard our sheep. Do not fear for me. The sun comes back, and I shall come back. May Mother Earth guard you." Then he drove away, and his wife watched him.

title: A father's words to his son

plan.english: The father said to his son, "Hear my words. Do not lie to your guest, and do not flee from the spear. If you do this, your fame will be great. Now go, and may the gods protect you." He heard the words and went away.

The mother said, "Son, you are going to the spears, and my heart trembles. Wear this clothing. Remember my words." "Mother, do not fear. I shall come back, and you will hear of my fame." Then he went out, and she stood there.

The sister came and said, "Brother, where are you going?" He answered, "Sister, I am going over the sea." "Drink the water, and take this gift. Remember your sister. May Sky guard your path, and come back with good fame." He drank the water, took the gift, and went.

title: The dying king and his sons

plan.english: The king lay down, and his sons came to him. He said, "Sons, I leave you my spears and my horses. Be brothers, and do not break the oath. Remember me. Sleep is coming to me."

title: The hero takes leave of his horses

plan.english: The hero led his horses to the field and spoke to them, "Swift horses, you who carried me for many nights, now lie down. Eat the grain, and drink the water. No one shall yoke you." The horses looked at him, and he went away.

title: The hero leaves his son to the gods

plan.english: The hero went out and spoke to Father Sky and Mother Earth, "Hear me, you gods! I give you my son. Guard him in the home. If I die, let him hear my name, and let him say, 'My fame is good.'"

title: The exile leaves his father's house

plan.english: The man left his home. He sat down and cried out, "My door! My fire! My field! I go away, and I shall not come back. May the gods guard you, and may no one burn you."
The wife answered him, "Go. I shall guard the fire, and the grain will grow. Remember me. May your spear be strong, and may your horses be swift. Come back to me."

title: The last night before the spears

plan.english: Two warriors were sitting by the fire in the night. This one said to that one, "At dawn the spears will drink. If I die, tell my mother, 'He did not flee.'" That one answered, "I shall tell her. You are famous." They drank, and they lay down.

The hero stood before the settlement and spoke to the dog, "Dog, you who guarded my settlement, sit down. Guard my wife and my sheep. May the wolf not come to the settlement. I go, and I shall come back." The dog heard him and lay down.

Dawn became bright, and the hero, grasping his spear, drew the horses. His dear ones stood and said, "May the wheel of the sun go before you. May you win great fame." "Guard our home." Then the horses ran forward, and they stood there.

The sons laid their father on the fire. The fire burned, and they spoke, "Go, father, by the path of the sun. May Mother Earth receive you. Your fame is imperishable. We shall remember your name." Then they went away.
